rows.title: Cascada 1.6L Turbo (Opel SIDI) Timing Chain & Carbon Buildup

rows.title: Water Pump Leak / Coolant Loss on 3.6L V6

rows.title: Rear A/C Evaporator Corrosion & Refrigerant Leaks

rows.title: Torque Converter Clutch (TCC) Shudder

rows.title: Encore 1.4L Turbo (LUJ/LUV) Timing Chain Stretch

rows.title: Excessive Oil Consumption on 2.4L Ecotec
rows.howToFix: GM TSB diagnostic involves an oil consumption test; remedies range from PCV/valve cover updates to piston and ring replacement. Owners commonly manage it by checking oil frequently and topping off, or rebuilding the short block in severe cases.

rows.title: Rear Suspension Toe Link Corrosion / Fracture (Salt-Belt Recall)
rows.howToFix: Under recall, dealers replace the rear suspension toe links and adjuster fasteners at no cost. Out of recall scope, replace corroded toe links with new parts.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Timing Chain / Tensioner Failure on 2.0T Turbo (LHU/LNF)
rows.howToFix: Replace the timing chain, tensioner, guides and any damaged valvetrain components; severe cases require partial or full engine rebuild. Preventively, change oil more frequently (~5,000 miles) and address any P0008/P0016/P0017 codes immediately before the chain jumps time.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Sudden Loss of Electric Power Steering Assist (Recall)
rows.howToFix: Under recall 21510, dealers replace the electric belt-drive rack-and-pinion steering gear assembly free of charge. Non-recall failures require diagnosis of the steering rack motor/module and replacement.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Non-recall failures require diagnosis of the steering rack motor/module and replacement.

rows.dispositionReason: The prescribed remedy is dealer, campaign, recall, or software work.

rows.title: Loss of Power Brake Assist — EBCM Software Defect (Recall)
rows.howToFix: Dealers reprogram/update the EBCM software at no cost; no replacement parts required. Owners should verify the recall has been completed via VIN.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Owners should verify the recall has been completed via VIN.

rows.dispositionReason: The prescribed remedy is dealer, campaign, recall, or software work.

rows.title: Estate Wagon Rear Self-Leveling Air Shock and Compressor Failure
rows.howToFix: Diagnose first: inspect the height sensor wiring under the driver-side rear seat for broken/corroded wires, test the sensor, and check the air lines for leaks at the shock fittings. If the shocks themselves leak, the most common modern fix is a conversion kit (Strutmasters CADR3 or similar) that replaces the air shocks with passive gas shocks and either deletes the air system or splits compressor output to aftermarket air bags via a T-fitting. Replace the compressor relay or compressor if it sticks on. Many owners simply unplug the compressor and run conventional shocks to eliminate the system entirely.

rows.title: 4L60E automatic transmission wear (valve body, sprag, harsh shift/no downshift)
rows.howToFix: For early valve-body symptoms, a valve body rebuild/updated valves and a fluid/filter service may suffice. For slipping or sprag/clutch failure, a full rebuild with upgraded hard parts (sunshell, sprag) is the accepted fix.
rows.dispositionReason: The remedy is a service, tool, consumable, or fluid procedure rather than a repair part.

rows.title: ABS hydraulic modulator corrosion / front brake fluid leak (safety recall)
rows.howToFix: Have the ABS modulator inspected and, if corroded/leaking, replaced (the recall remedy). Verify recall completion by VIN. Out-of-warranty, the modulator can be replaced with a known-good used or rebuilt unit and the system bled.

rows.title: Fuel pump / in-tank check valve failure causing hard starting and low pressure
rows.howToFix: Verify fuel pressure with a gauge (prime and leak-down test) before condemning the pump. Replace the in-tank fuel pump/sending-unit module (check valve is integral); inspect the pressure relief valve. The sending unit shares the module, so a weak float/gauge reading often accompanies pump wear.

rows.title: LT1 intake manifold gasket coolant/oil leak
rows.howToFix: Check and re-torque intake manifold bolts to spec first. If leaking persists, replace the intake manifold gaskets (and seals). Inspect for coolant contamination and top-end cleanliness during the job.

rows.title: Optispark (Opti-Spark) distributor failure on the LT1
rows.howToFix: Replace the Optispark with an AC Delco (vented) unit, and because the water pump has to come off to access it, replace the water pump at the same time. Ensure the distributor vent hoses are correctly routed and clear so condensation can escape. Rule out spark plug wires and plugs first, as those often mimic Optispark failure.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Reverse-flow cooling: water pump shaft seal leak and air-lock overheating
rows.howToFix: Replace the water pump (use special seal tool J39087 if only resealing, otherwise install a complete pump). When refilling coolant, open the bleeder screw on the thermostat housing to purge trapped air. Address any weep promptly to protect the Optispark below it.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.
